text:
Buffalo played the better game and lost it by three goals. The Sabres outchanced Columbus 2.85 to 2.12 in expected goals, took 56 shot attempts to 39, and deserved to win in 63 percent of simulated replays. The gap came down to a 54-second burst at the end of the first period. Matthew Knies scored on the power play at 17:58, and Adam Fantilli deflected one in at 18:44 to make it 3-1, a goal that carried only a 7 percent chance of going in. Mattias Samuelsson had given Buffalo the lead, and Cole Sillinger tied it, so the Sabres went to the room trailing after their weakest period of the night (0.55 expected goals to 1.10).

Buffalo took over the middle frame, outchancing Columbus 1.73 to 0.47, but converted only twice. Jack Quinn cut the deficit to one early, then Knies tipped in a 9 percent chance, and Konsta Helenius answered again. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen finished 2.88 goals worse than expected, while Jet Greaves was roughly average, 0.15 below expectation, on 26 shots. Columbus went 2 for 3 on the power play and Buffalo went 0 for 5, with the Sabres taking 11 penalty minutes to the Blue Jackets' 15.

Sean Monahan's power-play goal made it 5-3 in the third, and Mathieu Olivier closed it with a shot that had no measurable chance of scoring. Knies finished with two goals and an assist, Zach Werenski logged 28:48 and set up two, and Charlie Coyle assisted on three, including the first and last of Columbus's late goals. The Blue Jackets scored on the chances they got, and the Sabres could not return the favor.
